_rBO8neWw04.summary: Technology Connections explains how dishwashers work, why detergent pods underperform powder, and how to use the pre-wash and main-wash compartments. It argues you don't need to pre-rinse dishes.
_rBO8neWw04.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as the definitive, mind-changing explanation of dishwasher use, even though it runs over 30 minutes.

_ahvzDzKdB0.summary: Guy Steele's 1998 OOPSLA keynote on designing a programming language that its users can grow. He builds the talk using only one-syllable words and terms he has defined, to demonstrate the idea.
_ahvzDzKdB0.why: HN considers it one of the best technical talks ever and cites it in discussions of language design, small cores and extensibility.

_tpB-B8BXk0.summary: A short excerpt from Dr Russell Barkley's 2012 Burnett Lecture on ADHD, focused on treatment. He argues ADHD is a disorder of executive function and self-regulation, and that environments should be designed to compensate.
_tpB-B8BXk0.why: HN people with ADHD or ADHD-affected relatives share it as an authoritative, practical talk that helped some seek diagnosis.

_ZG8HBuDjgc.summary: Douglas Adams gives a talk at UCSB, recorded shortly before his death, about the odd lives of animals and what they suggest about humanity's future. It draws on his Last Chance to See work and is funny and wide-ranging.
_ZG8HBuDjgc.why: Adams fans repeatedly call it one of his best talks, a funny and moving look at extinction and the environment.

_Cp-BGQfpHQ.summary: AvE tears down the Juicero cold-press juicer, examining its heavily machined parts, electronics and the pricey juice packs. He pokes fun at the product and venture-funded culture along the way.
_Cp-BGQfpHQ.why: HN treats it as the classic teardown and the go-to example of over-engineered hardware built without real-world constraints.

_YWMGuh15nE.summary: Elevated is a 4 kilobyte PC demo by RGBA and TBC from Breakpoint 2009. It fly-throughs a realistic procedurally generated landscape with synthesized music and post-processing, all from a tiny executable.
_YWMGuh15nE.why: HN repeatedly holds it up as the benchmark for what procedural generation and size-coding can achieve in 4K.

_ivqWN4L3zU.summary: Bill Hammack of engineerguy explains how medieval engineers designed stone cathedrals using rules of thumb, with no science, mathematics or literacy. He uses it to define the engineering method.
_ivqWN4L3zU.why: HN recommends the series as a thoughtful account of engineering as rule-of-thumb problem solving that predates formal science.

_yMMTVVJI4c.summary: Technology Connections explains why electric kettles are uncommon in the US, centering on 120V circuits limiting power. He tests ways of boiling water on gas, electric ranges and kettles.
_yMMTVVJI4c.why: HN cites it constantly in threads on voltage, gas stoves and boiling water as the definitive measured comparison, with the kettle coming out fastest and most efficient.

_2LEgowbzSc.summary: Ed March rides a Honda C90 through Iran on his journey from Malaysia to the UK, showing the country and its people. He argues Iran is far more welcoming than the press suggests.
_2LEgowbzSc.why: Recommended for its heartwarming picture of Iranian hospitality toward a foreign rider.

_3loq22TxSc.summary: Tom Wildenhain's guest lecture for CMU's Esoteric Programming Languages course shows that PowerPoint transitions and slides are Turing complete without macros, building up to a mind-bending fractal ending.
_3loq22TxSc.why: Repeatedly recommended in best-talks threads as a fun, mind-blowing demonstration of unexpected computation.

_gXlauRB1EQ.summary: People Make Games investigates how Roblox relies on young, often child, developers to build its content while paying them very little. It covers Roblox's monetization model, the revenue split, and the harms to kids who make games on the platform.
_gXlauRB1EQ.why: HN commenters cite it as the go-to evidence that Roblox exploits child developers, and parents are pointed to it before letting kids build games there.

_-mBeYC2KGc.summary: Technology Connections explains why single-hose portable air conditioners are inefficient and often a poor choice compared with window units. It details how the single hose pulls in warm outside air and wastes energy.
_-mBeYC2KGc.why: The go-to recommendation to watch before buying a portable AC, cited in nearly every thread on cooling.

_L3gNaAVjQ4.summary: Lex Fridman interviews George Hotz, founder of Comma.ai, in a three-hour conversation. Topics include self-driving, Tesla and Waymo, crypto, GPT-3, immortality and book recommendations.
_L3gNaAVjQ4.why: Commenters recommend it as an entertaining, wide-ranging interview, and cite it for Hotz's views on end-to-end neural-net driving.

_P9HqHVPeik.summary: Stephen Wolfram gives a 13-minute tour of the Wolfram Language, a symbolic, functional programming language with a built-in knowledgebase. He demos querying large datasets, interactivity and deployment.
_P9HqHVPeik.why: Commenters point to it as a compact, impressive demo of what the language can do.

_bDXXWQxK38.summary: Real Engineering's Brian McManus explains Helion's approach to nuclear fusion: colliding two plasma rings, compressing them magnetically, and capturing energy directly from the changing magnetic flux rather than boiling water. It covers why this pulsed design sidesteps problems of tokamaks and laser fusion.
_bDXXWQxK38.why: It is the go-to accessible explainer whenever HN discusses Helion or alternative fusion designs.

_bP80DEAbuo.summary: Benn Jordan investigates infrasound and low-frequency noise from data centers, including xAI's Colossus and a crypto mine, and reports his own experiments on the effects. The video covers the health and community impacts on nearby residents.
_bP80DEAbuo.why: Cited in data center siting debates as evidence that noise and infrasound can seriously affect people living nearby.

_160oMzblY8.summary: Anders Brownworth gives a basic visual introduction to blockchain using an interactive web demo, covering SHA256 hashes, blocks, chains, distribution, tokens and coinbase transactions.
_160oMzblY8.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as the best ground-up, non-hype introduction for people who want to understand what a blockchain actually is.

_6pl5GG8RQ4.summary: Segment co-founder and CEO Peter Reinhardt recounts how his company found product-market fit, including how a product grew out of a small feature of another. It is a lecture from Stanford's Startup School course.
_6pl5GG8RQ4.why: HN founders recommend it as a must-watch on recognizing real product-market fit and avoiding solutions in search of problems.

_8bhtEgB8Mo.summary: A Royal Institution event with Sean Carroll and Jennifer Ouellette on what happens if you fall into a black hole, covering the firewall paradox, the information problem and the holographic principle.
_8bhtEgB8Mo.why: Recommended as a high-level but clear explanation of the black hole information paradox and competing theories, by a physicist known for making quantum mechanics approachable.

_DTpQ4Kk2wA.summary: A 1975 live demonstration of the APL language by Imperial College professor Bob Spence, showing a REPL on a modified typewriter terminal and APL's appeal to non-programmers.
_DTpQ4Kk2wA.why: Recommended as a charming, from-zero introduction to APL and a window into early interactive computing.

_IgqJr8jG8M.summary: Jon Purdy's Stanford EE380 seminar giving an overview of concatenative programming, from function composition theory and history down to low-level implementation and correctness benefits.
_IgqJr8jG8M.why: HN recommends it as the best talk on concatenative languages and their mathematical properties.

_fHfgU8oMSo.summary: A Deadspin compilation of local news anchors at Sinclair-owned stations reading the same scripted message about irresponsible one-sided news. It was assembled by Timothy Burke.
_fHfgU8oMSo.why: HN cites it as a vivid example of media consolidation and coordinated messaging.

_ul7X5js1vE.summary: Stevie Wonder performs 'Superstition' on Sesame Street in 1973, with kids dancing along. It is a feel-good live music performance.
_ul7X5js1vE.why: Recommended in Sesame Street and children's TV threads as a favorite example of the show's funkier past.

_7X6Yeydgyg.summary: A 69-minute documentary on the Polybius arcade-game legend. It examines visual, physical and anecdotal evidence, traces the story's source, and concludes the game never existed beyond one website entry.
_7X6Yeydgyg.why: HN rates it among the best gaming video essays and Ahoy as one of the best creators on the platform.

_9B__0S21y8.summary: Hillel Wayne's Strange Loop talk introducing TLA+ as a specification language for finding concurrency bugs in designs. It covers stalling, race conditions and dropped messages, with PlusCal examples.
_9B__0S21y8.why: Recommended as a concise, high-level intro to what TLA+ is and when it helps.

_KRb_qV9P4g.summary: Animator Noodle explains why frame interpolation does not make animation better, covering timing, easing, smear frames and using the wrong tool for the job. A pinned correction says the video is partly outdated given later AI developments.
_KRb_qV9P4g.why: HN commenters recommend it in motion-smoothing and interpolation threads as an overview of why interpolation hurts animation.

_fQtxKmgJC8.summary: Gaming Historian recounts how Alexey Pajitnov created Tetris in the Soviet Union and how a fight over publishing rights spanned the West, Mirrorsoft, Nintendo and the Cold War. It runs about an hour with chaptered parts.
_fQtxKmgJC8.why: HN recommends it as an excellent documentary on Tetris and its tangled licensing history.

_o7qjN3KF8U.summary: A KRAZAM satirical sketch about hustle culture and productivity obsession in tech.
_o7qjN3KF8U.why: HN posts it as a joke in productivity and focus threads, and some praise the channel as pitch-perfect satire of tech stereotypes.

_x0eyNkNpL0.summary: Slavoj Zizek discusses his book Violence in an Authors@Google talk in New York. He covers ideology, including his idea of the unknown knowns.
_x0eyNkNpL0.why: Recommended as a relatively clear introduction to Zizek's thinking, especially his account of ideology and unknown knowns.

_BNIkw4Ao9w.summary: Troy Hunt argues that even static, non-secret websites need HTTPS, demonstrating attacks such as injected content and China's Great Cannon. It accompanies his blog post of the same name.
_BNIkw4Ao9w.why: Cited as a must-watch persuasive case for HTTPS everywhere.

_Cm6EFYktRQ.summary: Part 4 of the BBS: The Documentary series, covering FidoNet, the amateur network that linked dial-up bulletin board systems together to relay messages and files worldwide.
_Cm6EFYktRQ.why: Recommended as a great documentary on FidoNet's rise, with interviews with figures like Tom Jennings.

__wn9zXFiy8.summary: A two-hour NANOG tutorial by Richard Steenbergen aimed at network engineers, covering optical networking technologies. This is the updated 2017 edition of a recurring talk.
__wn9zXFiy8.why: Commenters call it an invaluable, approachable way to learn how optical networking actually works.

_gXiVOmaVSo.summary: A Foresight Institute workshop video with two talks: Shawn Douglas on nanoscale instruments for visualizing small proteins, and Bret Victor on Dynamicland. Victor's part shows biomolecular design built in his Realtalk system with physical objects.
_gXiVOmaVSo.why: HN points to Bret Victor's segment as a recent, concrete demonstration of Dynamicland's ideas applied to a specific scientific domain.

_zSjpIyMt0k.summary: A one-minute capture of Tim Clarke's 1993 'Mars' DOS demo, a roughly 5 KB program that renders a navigable terrain landscape in real time.
_zSjpIyMt0k.why: Remembered fondly as a tiny, efficient demo that inspired graphics programmers and is a benchmark for modern terrain rendering.

_zfN9wnPvU0.summary: Kurzgesagt examines how AI-generated content is flooding the internet, from video and music to news and books. It looks at how this makes verifying what is real harder.
_zfN9wnPvU0.why: HN uses it as a reference for AI slop, LLMs citing LLM output, and the growing difficulty of fact checking.

_0QMKFzW9fw.summary: Physicist Angela Collier rants for 42 minutes about why violin plots are a poor way to show data, citing papers on violin and bean plots. It is part lecture on how to read distributions and part opinionated critique.
_0QMKFzW9fw.why: HN links it in data-visualization threads as an entertaining case against violin plots.

_9mzmvhwMqw.summary: Sophie Wilson, designer of the ARM instruction set, discusses the future of microprocessors, including the economics of scaling below 28nm and why much of a chip must stay powered off.
_9mzmvhwMqw.why: HN commenters cite it for the claim that process scaling beyond 28nm is uneconomic and for dark silicon.

_ArVh3Cj9rw.summary: Vsauce explores how human reasoning works, drawing on the social theory of reason and the extended mind thesis, made in partnership with Bill Gates around climate change.
_ArVh3Cj9rw.why: HN commenters cite it for the social theory that reasoning evolved as a collaborative activity, and one lists it as a favorite video.

_B_4vhsmRRI.summary: Marco Baringer's tutorial video on SLIME, the Emacs mode for developing Common Lisp. It demonstrates the interactive workflow of working against a live Lisp image.
_B_4vhsmRRI.why: HN points to it to show what the Lisp REPL workflow is like and as a good tour of SLIME.

_GVSLcqGP7g.summary: Modern Vintage Gamer looks at OpenLara, an open source Tomb Raider engine, running on the Game Boy Advance. The video explains how the port achieves playable speeds on the GBA's slow ARM CPU, with input from the developer XProger.
_GVSLcqGP7g.why: HN points to it as coverage of an impressive 3D game port on very limited hardware.

_NuvwndwYSY.summary: CuriousMarc inspects a newly arrived Teletype Model 19, an early military unit built around a Model 15 keyboard and printer, after an initial rough cleaning. It is the first part of a restoration series and touches on 5-bit Baudot code.
_NuvwndwYSY.why: HN commenters point to this restoration series as a thorough explanation of how teletypes work at every level.

_YysNM2JoFo.summary: A Numberphile video with Dr James Grime on Sloane's Gap, the observation that integers in the OEIS are not evenly represented and some numbers are underrepresented. It explains the clusters of 'interesting' numbers.
_YysNM2JoFo.why: HN recommends it as a concise, quick explanation of the OEIS pattern when threads touch the integer sequence encyclopedia.

_b4qKv1Ctv8.summary: A long conversation between Eric Weinstein and Daniel Schmachtenberger on whether humanity can flourish long term on a single planet, introducing the Game A versus Game B framing. It covers catastrophic risk and alternatives to rivalrous systems.
_b4qKv1Ctv8.why: Commenters recommend the whole interview as a wide-ranging discussion of existential risk.

_fZOl7C_vDI.summary: A reading of David Foster Wallace's essay Consider the Lobster, about the 2003 Maine Lobster Festival and the ethics of boiling lobsters alive. The reading runs about 50 minutes.
_fZOl7C_vDI.why: Linked in threads about lobster welfare as an easy way to take in Wallace's essay.

_loUDS4c3Cs.summary: A filmmaker explains why the Apollo moon landing footage could not have been faked in a studio, based on the video and film technology of the late 1960s. He walks through the limits of cameras, frame rates and effects of the era.
_loUDS4c3Cs.why: HN points to it as a concise, technically grounded rebuttal to moon-hoax claims.

_2khAmMTAjI.summary: A Second Thought video arguing that the CIA is responsible for serious crimes, coups and unrest around the world, with historical examples and further reading.
_2khAmMTAjI.why: HN commenters cite it as a source for US-backed coups and foreign policy contradictions, and as an example of a video they say YouTube suppressed.

_Qd3erAPI9w.summary: A Veritasium video on survivor bias, explaining how an observed sample can be incomplete and skewed. It uses examples such as bombers and famous success stories.
_Qd3erAPI9w.why: HN uses it as a handy reference whenever a thread needs to point at survivorship bias.

_eSAF_qT_FY.summary: Christopher Domas's Black Hat talk demonstrates a hardware backdoor in a third-party x86 processor, a hidden core that grants root from userland. He uses it to discuss how feasible broader hardware backdoors might be.
_eSAF_qT_FY.why: Cited in hardware-trust and supply-chain threads as a concrete, startling demonstration of chip-level backdoors.

_-agl0pOQfs.summary: The official music video for Insane Clown Posse's song Miracles, from the album Bang Pow Boom.
_-agl0pOQfs.why: Mostly posted as a joke in threads on magnets and physics, echoing the song's 'magnets' lyric.

_2NI6t2r_Hs.summary: Rob Pike gives an insider's account of the history of Unix and the development of key pieces of modern computing, including Bell Labs anecdotes.
_2NI6t2r_Hs.why: Mostly cited as a source of Unix history stories and asides such as the Crabs prank program and the BLIT terminal.

_6sh097Dk5k.summary: Dave Jaggar, who defined much of the ARM architecture, recounts how Acorn's near-extinction led to ARM, including the history of Thumb, StrongARM, and the Austin team.
_6sh097Dk5k.why: HN cites it for first-hand ARM history, including Thumb's origin, and for Jaggar's endorsement of RISC-V.

_7vPNcnYWQ4.summary: Stuff Made Here designs and builds an "unpickable" lock, then calls in a locksmith to see if it can be defeated. It covers the mechanical design effort and the attempt to pick it.
_7vPNcnYWQ4.why: Raised in lock-picking threads as a related attempt at an unpickable lock, and for novel anti-picking mechanisms.

_9LX9HSQkWo.summary: Corridor Crew explain how they made an anime short by filming themselves and running the footage through custom-trained Stable Diffusion models. The video walks through the technique and its open-source foundations.
_9LX9HSQkWo.why: HN cites it as an example of temporally stable AI video stylization built from ordinary production gear.

_ByEBjf9ktY.summary: Not Just Bikes explains why crossing streets is dangerous in the US and Canada, where roads are designed to move cars fast, and contrasts it with Dutch designs for pedestrians.
_ByEBjf9ktY.why: Linked in road-safety threads as a good explanation of how street and signal design prevent pedestrian deaths.

_DrsVhzbLzU.summary: A BBC Question Time clip in which Ian Hislop argues against capital punishment, rebutting the deterrence argument. He points out the problem of executing innocent people.
_DrsVhzbLzU.why: Cited in threads on wrongful convictions and executions as a pithy rebuttal of the deterrence argument.

_gZK0tW8EhQ.summary: Ron Garret tells the story of the Remote Agent Experiment on NASA's Deep Space 1, where autonomous software controlled a spacecraft in 1999. He describes debugging Lisp code remotely from millions of miles away.
_gZK0tW8EhQ.why: Cited in Lisp and safety-critical software threads as the definitive firsthand account of the DS1 remote REPL debugging episode.

_mP9OmOFxc4.summary: Joe Rogan interviews Jack Dorsey, then CEO of Twitter and Square, for about two hours. They discuss Twitter's value, moderation, misinformation and echo chambers.
_mP9OmOFxc4.why: HN uses it as a source on Dorsey's views on Twitter moderation, with mixed opinions on how well he answered censorship questions.

_njf8jwEGRo.summary: Robert Sapolsky's Stanford lecture on chaos and reductionism, which he calls one of the hardest of the course. It examines the limits of breaking systems into parts to understand them and introduces chaotic systems.
_njf8jwEGRo.why: Pointed to as a clear statement of irreducible complexity, the limits of reductionism, and why simple neuron-level explanations fall short.

_ve4M4UsJQo.summary: Honda's 2003 'Cog' commercial for the Accord, a two-minute Rube Goldberg chain reaction of car parts. It was filmed practically rather than with CGI.
_ve4M4UsJQo.why: Cited as an ad worth enjoying and as an example of practical effects so good they were mistaken for CGI.

_2GT2PCUN3Q.summary: A four-minute programmer rap by stdout about abandoned side projects and the promise to finish them someday. The lyrics poke fun at dev procrastination and big app ideas.
_2GT2PCUN3Q.why: HN shares it as a relatable, funny song when threads turn to the struggle of finishing side projects.

_3P_S7pL7Yg.summary: Tom Scott visits an eHighway test in Lubeck, Germany, where electric trucks with pantographs draw power from overhead wires. He explains how this could electrify road freight.
_3P_S7pL7Yg.why: The standard reference whenever threads discuss electrifying trucking via overhead lines instead of big batteries.

_47utWAoupo.summary: A one-minute clip of a Volvo automatic braking demonstration that fails to stop. The uploader finds it funny.
_47utWAoupo.why: HN cites it as an example of the limits of driver-assist safety systems, often with the caveat that the pedestrian-detection option was not fitted.

_8fU2QG-lV0.summary: An h3h3Productions video on the CSGO gambling scandal involving the YouTubers ProSyndicate and TmarTn, who promoted a gambling site they owned without disclosing it.
_8fU2QG-lV0.why: HN cites it as a record of the CSGO gambling controversy and of undisclosed influencer ownership.

_8yVOC4ciXc.summary: Rob Miles discusses GPT-3 on Computerphile, covering how scaling parameters kept improving results over GPT-2 and how the model nearly learned arithmetic without anyone knowing exactly how.
_8yVOC4ciXc.why: HN commenters cite it as a concise explanation of GPT-3's scaling jump and surprising abilities at its release.

_BgJEXQkjNQ.summary: USLaunchReport footage of the September 2016 SpaceX Falcon 9 static fire anomaly that destroyed the rocket and AMOS-6 satellite at Launch Complex 40.
_BgJEXQkjNQ.why: HN people link it as the reference footage of the earlier SpaceX pad explosion when discussing later launch failures.

_EUPwsD64GI.summary: A one-minute clip from Who Framed Roger Rabbit in which a swinging pendant lamp is bumped and keeps flailing, showing animators' attention to detail.
_EUPwsD64GI.why: Used as an example of going the extra mile on small details in animation and design.

_FjuPn7MXMs.summary: A short demo of a 3D Wayland compositor built with Qt 5 and QtWayland, mapping input to and compositing the output of Wayland applications in a 3D scene, also running on a Raspberry Pi.
_FjuPn7MXMs.why: Cited as an existing example of 3D or spatial desktop shells and what Wayland compositing makes possible.

_Gsz7Gu6agA.summary: A scene from The Sopranos in which two old-school mobsters try to extort a Starbucks and learn that electronic payments leave an indisputable record of sales.
_Gsz7Gu6agA.why: HN posts it jokingly in threads about payments, taxes and cash, as a funny illustration of how digital transactions make low-level shenanigans harder.

_HbVWm7wdmE.summary: A three-minute clip about Ernst Dickmanns' VaMoR and VaMP projects, in which fully autonomous vehicles drove thousands of miles on public roads in the 1980s. It is a brief look at early German self-driving research.
_HbVWm7wdmE.why: HN commenters cite it as proof that autonomous driving was demonstrated decades before the current boom.

_IqWal_EmBg.summary: Air traffic audio of a pilot slurring and incoherent while declaring an emergency due to extreme hypoxia, with controllers at Cleveland Center struggling to understand him.
_IqWal_EmBg.why: Cited as an audible example of what hypoxia sounds like and how consciousness fades gradually.

_K-L9uhsBLM.summary: A short clip from The Office US in which Kevin decides talking normally wastes time and starts abbreviating all his words and sentences, confusing his coworkers. It is a sitcom scene from Season 8, Episode 2.
_K-L9uhsBLM.why: Used as a punchline whenever HN threads touch on terse communication, token-saving prompts or verbose writing.

_K0tXOBPMHA.summary: Seattle Police Department compilation of open-source video of violent incidents in the Capitol Hill Occupied Protest (CHOP) zone in 2020, released around the July 1 emergency proclamation.
_K0tXOBPMHA.why: HN uses it as a reference for footage of shootings in the CHOP zone, cited as evidence in political arguments.

_LiDTKEF1ek.summary: A one-minute clip of David Mitchell on a UK panel show explaining why he respects poor customer service in Britain. He argues that people who do their job well should not also be required to be nice.
_LiDTKEF1ek.why: Cited in threads about forced enthusiasm and 'service with a smile' in the workplace.

_LjN3UclYzU.summary: A short hip-hop remix of the well-known 'The missile knows where it is' monologue about missile guidance logic. It is a meme-style piece taken from 4chan.
_LjN3UclYzU.why: Used as a joke whenever a thread touches on missile guidance or Kalman filters.

_NzVmtbPOrM.summary: Tom Scott explains why a vivid pink pigment by artist Stuart Semple cannot be fully shown on a screen, and touches on the dispute over exclusive rights to the blackest black pigment. It is a short explainer on color gamuts and pigment politics.
_NzVmtbPOrM.why: Cited as an example of colors too vibrant for monitors and pigments outside the sRGB gamut.

_OwG_rQ_Hqw.summary: A Computer History Museum recording of the final demonstration of the Xerox Star, the early graphical user interface workstation. It is a long demo session that shows the design thinking behind desktop, icons and windows.
_OwG_rQ_Hqw.why: HN people point to it as a primary-source look at Star's interface design, especially its philosophy of fewer commands without fewer functions.

_Pz3syET3DY.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on the American prison system, covering conditions, private prison economics and more, with comedic framing.
_Pz3syET3DY.why: Cited as a reference when HN threads discuss US prisons, for-profit incarceration, and obstacles after release.

_QST1ZAJ29o.summary: Footage of the 1985 world premiere of the Amiga 1000 at Lincoln Center. It shows demos such as multitasking and the bouncing ball, and Andy Warhol painting Debbie Harry live on the machine.
_QST1ZAJ29o.why: Cited in Amiga threads as the source for the Warhol live-painting moment and the launch event.

_QvguJJNilA.summary: Neil and Laura Westwood pitch their Magic Whiteboard, reusable static-cling whiteboard sheets, to the investors on the BBC's Dragons' Den and win 100,000 pounds of investment.
_QvguJJNilA.why: Mentioned as a UK example of a whiteboard product that took off after a Dragons' Den appearance, in threads about whiteboard products.

_XneTBhRPYk.summary: A CBC The National investigation into Apple's business practices, including undercover work on repair pricing and the battery slowdown scandal. It examines allegations of overpriced repairs and misdiagnosis.
_XneTBhRPYk.why: Cited in threads on Apple repair and battery policies as evidence of questionable repair practices, rather than recommended as a must-watch.

_ZBKX-6Gz6A.summary: A CBC satire sketch in which a self-proclaimed thought leader gives a talk full of empty gestures and nothing-saying inspiration. It parodies TED-style conference talks.
_ZBKX-6Gz6A.why: HN uses it as a joke or reference when mocking TED-style talks and thought-leader culture.

_ZI_aEalijE.summary: A fan-made video of the Simpsons Stonecutters Song, in which a secret society takes credit for controlling world affairs, with lyrics and stills from the show.
_ZI_aEalijE.why: Used purely as a joke reply when a thread touches on secret groups or conspiratorial control.

_ZIqdrFeFBk.summary: A subtitled 1958 clip of Egyptian president Gamal Abdel Nasser recounting, with laughter, a Muslim Brotherhood suggestion that women be required to wear a head covering.
_ZIqdrFeFBk.why: Posted as an archival counterexample in debates about Islam, headscarves and Egypt's politics.

__CvmS6uw7E.summary: A clip from a radio show in which Joe Rogan spars with a caller who claims to be a primatologist about bonobo apes, with Bill Burr present. It is a short comedy-radio exchange.
__CvmS6uw7E.why: HN mentions it mainly critically, as an example of Rogan spreading a claim later debunked.

_fNp37zFn9Q.summary: A Swedish fiber provider's short experiment in which volunteers wear Oculus Rift headsets that add lag to their view of real life. They try to do everyday tasks like making pancakes.
_fNp37zFn9Q.why: Cited as a funny illustration of how lag wrecks hand-eye coordination.

_fV-C1Ag5sI.summary: Empire Files host Mike Prysner responds point by point to John Oliver's Last Week Tonight episode on Venezuela, arguing it distorted the country's situation and the role of the US government.
_fV-C1Ag5sI.why: Cited, without much elaboration, by commenters who think mainstream media misinforms about Venezuela.

_hnOCUkbix0.summary: A short parody ad for the Lenovo X300 ultraportable, mocking the original MacBook Air ad.
_hnOCUkbix0.why: Mostly cited as a joke or as the commenter's old laptop, in threads about Apple laptops.

_iiOEQOtBlQ.summary: A short clip from the film Office Space in which Peter explains his typical workday to the Bobs, the consultants.
_iiOEQOtBlQ.why: Used as a joke reference in threads about slacking at work and workplace dysfunction.

_jyT1rnW9fA.summary: A short clip of Joe Biden describing how he pressed Ukraine to fire a prosecutor by threatening to withhold loan guarantees, framed by the uploader around Hunter Biden's board role.
_jyT1rnW9fA.why: Cited in political arguments as evidence of an alleged quid pro quo.

_m97_kL4ox0.summary: A 2007 Google Tech Talk introducing Polyworld, an artificial life simulator used to evolve artificial intelligence by designing worlds rather than minds. It presents results from ongoing attempts to evolve intelligent behavior.
_m97_kL4ox0.why: Referenced as an interesting early example of developing AI through evolution and artificial life simulation.

_o-HcG8QxPc.summary: Netflix engineer Drew Gallatin explains how Netflix serves TLS-encrypted video at 400Gb/s from a single FreeBSD server. He covers NUMA, kernel TLS, hardware TLS offload and the memory bandwidth and PCIe bottlenecks they hit.
_o-HcG8QxPc.why: HN cites it as a prime example of FreeBSD tuned for extreme network performance at massive scale.

_oJs8-I9WtA.summary: Technology Connections compares Betamax and VHS picture quality using footage from a 1979 RCA VCR and argues the Beta quality advantage was largely marketing.
_oJs8-I9WtA.why: Cited as evidence that Betamax was not meaningfully better than VHS.

_ogxZxu6cjM.summary: A short clip from The Wire in which police officers manipulate crime statistics to make the numbers look better. It dramatizes how metrics get gamed.
_ogxZxu6cjM.why: Used as a go-to illustration of Goodhart's law and statistical manipulation in institutions.

_sBBaNYex3E.summary: Boston Dynamics shows its Atlas humanoid robot performing a gymnastics and parkour routine, using optimization-generated motions and a model predictive controller.
_sBBaNYex3E.why: Used as a go-to demonstration of how far dynamic robot locomotion has come.

_wY7FBtr7_c.summary: Leandro Facchinetti explains why he thinks Racket is a great language and why he stopped using it. He describes his backstory and experiences with the Racket community.
_wY7FBtr7_c.why: Mostly cited critically, as evidence of problems in the Racket community, rather than recommended.
